\chapter{More Everyday Verbs}
\label{ch:ka-more-verbs}
\hlchaptermodality{43}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can tell someone to come, sit, stand and give in Kannada.}

Complete KA-C43-give and say all four verbs in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[bā]{\kn{ಬಾ} (bā) — come}

\label{lesson:KA-C43-come}



\begin{quote}
A short run of everyday verbs, one at a time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬಾ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಾ}} (\emph{bā}) — \textquotedblleft{}come\textquotedblright{}.

One syllable, and a whole sentence. The commonest thing said at a doorway.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{bā}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಬಾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}come\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kuḷitukō]{\kn{ಕುಳಿತುಕೋ} (kuḷitukō) — sit}

\label{lesson:KA-C43-sit}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{bā} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕುಳಿತುಕೋ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕುಳಿತುಕೋ}} (\emph{kuḷitukō}) — \textquotedblleft{}sit\textquotedblright{}.

Longer than it looks: the \emph{-ko} on the end is a reflexive, so it is closer to 'seat yourself' than to a bare order.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kuḷitukō}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{bā}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕುಳಿತುಕೋ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}sit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nillu]{\kn{ನಿಲ್ಲು} (nillu) — stand}

\label{lesson:KA-C43-stand}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{kuḷitukō} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ನಿಲ್ಲು}}
\textbf{\kn{ನಿಲ್ಲು}} (\emph{nillu}) — \textquotedblleft{}stand\textquotedblright{}.

The pair to sitting, and the bare stem again — Kannada asks for nothing extra to make a command.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{nillu}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{kuḷitukō}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ನಿಲ್ಲು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}stand\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[koḍu]{\kn{ಕೊಡು} (koḍu) — give}

\label{lesson:KA-C43-give}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{nillu} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕೊಡು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕೊಡು}} (\emph{koḍu}) — \textquotedblleft{}give\textquotedblright{}.

The everyday 'give'. Politeness is added with a separate word, not by altering this one.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. That closes the run: four everyday actions, each met on its own.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{koḍu}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{nillu}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕೊಡು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}give\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
